title: grammar-of-immunity: analysis code and manuscript for "Biologically informed TCR representations improve in-distribution prediction but fail to generalize to unseen epitopes"

creators.name: Tejkowski, Erick
creators.affiliation: Independent researcher, Fairview Heights, Illinois, USA

creators.name: Paredes, Maria Elisa
creators.affiliation: Independent researcher, Fairview Heights, Illinois, USA

description:
Analysis code, manuscript source and figures for a direct test of the hypothesis that segmenting TCR CDR3β along the boundaries created by V(D)J recombination — germline-contributed termini and the junctional N-region — yields receptor representations that generalize to epitopes absent from training.

Using 121,467 deduplicated human TCRβ clonotypes from VDJdb and the official IMMREP23 benchmark and metric, it does not. Junctional regions do carry reproducible order-dependent structure (+0.1013 AUC from (V,J) conditioning, of which +0.0392 survives a boundary-trim control), but on withheld epitopes every arm sits at chance, and the within-distribution advantage is explained almost entirely by germline V/J identity rather than junctional sequence. No method exceeds 0.52 Macro AUC0.1 on the seven unseen IMMREP23 peptides, including NetTCR-2.2 retrained on the identical split.

All analyses are implemented in the Python standard library, are deterministic under fixed seeds, and reproduce on a laptop in minutes. Third-party inputs (VDJdb, IMMREP23, NetTCR-2.2) are fetched rather than redistributed; see README.md.
